bank.name: Constitution & Politics
bank.subject: Pakistan Affairs
bank.description: The 1973 Constitution, its amendments, and Pakistan's political and judicial system.

questions.prompt: How many Articles does the 1973 Constitution of Pakistan contain?
questions.explanation: The 1973 Constitution consists of 280 Articles (plus schedules and annexes).

questions.prompt: Which system of government does the 1973 Constitution of Pakistan establish?
questions.explanation: The 1973 Constitution establishes a parliamentary (Westminster-style) system with the Prime Minister as head of government.

questions.prompt: Who is the head of state under the 1973 Constitution?
questions.explanation: The President is the head of state, elected by an electoral college of parliament and provincial assemblies.

questions.prompt: How many members does the National Assembly of Pakistan have?
questions.explanation: The National Assembly has 342 seats: 272 general, 60 reserved for women and 10 for minorities.

questions.prompt: Before the 26th Amendment, how many members did the Senate of Pakistan have?
questions.explanation: The Senate had 100 members before the 26th Amendment (2024) increased provincial representation.

questions.prompt: Which constitutional amendment renamed the North-West Frontier Province (NWFP) to Khyber Pakhtunkhwa?
questions.explanation: The 18th Amendment (2010) renamed NWFP to Khyber Pakhtunkhwa.

questions.prompt: In which year was the 18th Amendment passed?
questions.explanation: The 18th Amendment was passed in April 2010 and is the largest amendment to the constitution.

questions.prompt: Which amendment abolished the President's discretionary power to dissolve the National Assembly under Article 58(2)(b)?
questions.explanation: The 18th Amendment (2010) abolished Article 58(2)(b), shifting power to parliament and the Prime Minister.

questions.prompt: Which amendment merged the Federally Administered Tribal Areas (FATA) into Khyber Pakhtunkhwa?
questions.explanation: The 25th Amendment (2018) merged FATA into Khyber Pakhtunkhwa.

questions.prompt: According to the Objectives Resolution, sovereignty over the entire universe belongs to whom?
questions.explanation: The Objectives Resolution (1949) declared that sovereignty over the entire universe belongs to Almighty Allah alone.

questions.prompt: Which Constitution of Pakistan introduced a presidential system of government?
questions.explanation: The 1962 Constitution, promulgated by Ayub Khan, introduced a presidential system.

questions.prompt: What is the national language of Pakistan according to the 1973 Constitution?
questions.explanation: Article 251 declares Urdu as the national language, with regional languages to be promoted.

questions.prompt: Who can remove the President of Pakistan through impeachment?
questions.explanation: The President can be impeached for violation of the constitution or gross misconduct by a joint sitting of parliament with a two-thirds majority.

questions.prompt: Which body conducts general elections in Pakistan?
questions.explanation: The Election Commission of Pakistan (ECP), established under Article 218, conducts and supervises elections.

questions.prompt: In which year did Benazir Bhutto become the first woman Prime Minister of Pakistan?
questions.explanation: Benazir Bhutto became Prime Minister in December 1988, the first woman to head a Muslim-majority country's government.

questions.prompt: Who imposed martial law in Pakistan on 5 July 1977?
questions.explanation: General Muhammad Zia-ul-Haq imposed martial law on 5 July 1977 and remained in power until 1988.

questions.prompt: The doctrine by which courts validated otherwise unconstitutional actions of the executive is known as?
questions.explanation: The Doctrine of Necessity was invoked in 1958, 1969, 1977 and 1999 to validate martial law regimes.

questions.prompt: Which Article of the 1973 Constitution guarantees equality of all citizens before the law?
questions.explanation: Article 25 provides equality of citizens before the law and prohibits discrimination.

questions.prompt: How is the Prime Minister of Pakistan elected?
options: By a majority in the National Assembly
questions.explanation: The Prime Minister is elected by a majority of members in the National Assembly.

questions.prompt: Which amendment reduced the President's powers by restoring the parliamentary system and is often called a 'mini-constitution'?
questions.explanation: The 18th Amendment (2010) is often called a 'mini-constitution' for the sweeping changes it made.

questions.prompt: According to the 1973 Constitution, the state religion of Pakistan is?
questions.explanation: Islam is declared the state religion under Article 2 of the Constitution.

questions.prompt: The head of state of Pakistan is the?
questions.explanation: The President is the head of state; the Prime Minister is the head of government.

questions.prompt: The head of government of Pakistan is the?
questions.explanation: The Prime Minister heads the federal government under the 1973 Constitution.

questions.prompt: The Parliament of Pakistan consists of how many houses?
questions.explanation: Pakistan has a bicameral parliament: the National Assembly (lower house) and Senate (upper house).

questions.prompt: What is the maximum number of seats in the National Assembly?
questions.explanation: After the 25th Amendment, the National Assembly has 336 seats including reserved seats.

questions.prompt: Which article of the Constitution guarantees fundamental rights?
questions.explanation: Fundamental rights are enshrined in Articles 8-28 of the Constitution.

questions.prompt: The superior judiciary of Pakistan consists of?
options: The Supreme Court, Federal Shariat Court and High Courts
questions.explanation: The superior judiciary comprises the Supreme Court, Federal Shariat Court and provincial High Courts.

questions.prompt: The 18th Amendment (2010) is most famous for?
options: Devolving powers and abolishing the concurrent list
questions.explanation: The 18th Amendment devolved 17 ministries to provinces and abolished the concurrent list.

questions.prompt: The Council of Common Interests (CCI) was restored by which amendment?
questions.explanation: The 18th Amendment revived the CCI to resolve federal-provincial matters.

questions.prompt: Who is the Chairman of the Senate of Pakistan?
options: The Senate elects its own chairman
questions.explanation: The Senate elects its Chairman from among its members.

questions.prompt: The National Assembly speaker is elected by?
options: The members of the National Assembly
questions.explanation: Members of the National Assembly elect their own Speaker.

questions.prompt: How many seats are reserved for women in the National Assembly?
questions.explanation: 60 seats are reserved for women in the National Assembly (Article 51).

questions.prompt: The Senate of Pakistan has how many seats after the 25th Amendment?
questions.explanation: The Senate has 96 members after the 25th Amendment (2022) merged FATA.

questions.prompt: The term of the Senate is?
questions.explanation: Senators serve 6-year terms; half retire every three years.

questions.prompt: The term of the National Assembly is?
questions.explanation: The National Assembly sits for a 5-year term.

questions.prompt: Which amendment fixed the tenure of the Chief of Army Staff?
questions.explanation: The 19th Amendment set a uniform tenure for the army chief.

questions.prompt: The '22nd Amendment' (2016) is related to?
options: Appointment of the Chief Election Commissioner
questions.explanation: The 22nd Amendment addressed CEC appointment and the ECP.

questions.prompt: Which amendment merged FATA with Khyber Pakhtunkhwa?
questions.explanation: The 25th Amendment merged FATA into KP in 2018.

questions.prompt: Article 62 and 63 of the Constitution deal with?
questions.explanation: Articles 62-63 set the qualifications and disqualification criteria for legislators.

questions.prompt: The federal capital territory of Pakistan is?
questions.explanation: Islamabad Capital Territory is the federal capital area.

questions.prompt: How many provincial assemblies does Pakistan have?
questions.explanation: Each of the four provinces has its own provincial assembly.

questions.prompt: The 'National Command Authority' (NCA) is headed by?
questions.explanation: The PM chairs the NCA, which oversees Pakistan's nuclear assets.

questions.prompt: The Federal Shariat Court hears appeals on?
questions.explanation: The Federal Shariat Court reviews laws against Islamic injunctions.

questions.prompt: The 'Election Commission of Pakistan' conducts?
questions.explanation: The ECP conducts all national and provincial elections.

questions.prompt: What is the 'National Assembly' called in Urdu?
questions.explanation: The National Assembly is the Qaumi Assembly; the Senate is the upper house.

questions.prompt: The 'Majlis-e-Shura' in Islamic governance traditionally means?
questions.explanation: Majlis-e-Shura is the consultative assembly in Islamic political tradition.

questions.prompt: Which schedule of the Constitution lists the federal legislative subjects?
questions.explanation: The Fourth Schedule lists federal subjects; the Fifth, provincial subjects.

questions.prompt: The President of Pakistan is elected by?
options: An electoral college of parliament and provincial assemblies
questions.explanation: The President is elected by an electoral college comprising MPs and provincial legislators.

questions.prompt: Article 245 of the Constitution deals with?
options: The Armed Forces and their role in defending Pakistan
questions.explanation: Article 245 concerns the Armed Forces' duty to defend Pakistan.

questions.prompt: Who was the first President of the Constituent Assembly of Pakistan?
questions.explanation: Jinnah served as the first President of the Constituent Assembly until his death.

questions.prompt: Which article of the 1973 Constitution deals with the independence of the judiciary?
questions.explanation: Article 175 states that the judiciary shall be separate from the executive.

questions.prompt: How many times was the 1973 Constitution suspended or abrogated?
questions.explanation: It was suspended under martial law in 1977 and 1999.

questions.prompt: Who administers the oath of office to the Prime Minister?
questions.explanation: The President administers the oath to the Prime Minister under Article 91.

questions.prompt: The National Assembly has how many general seats?
questions.explanation: There are 266 general seats plus 60 reserved for women and 10 for minorities, totalling 336.

questions.prompt: Which constitutional amendment lowered the voting age from 21 to 18?
questions.explanation: The 18th Amendment (2010) also reduced the voting age to 18.

questions.prompt: Who can dissolve the National Assembly under the 1973 Constitution?
options: The President on the Prime Minister's advice
questions.explanation: Under Article 58, the President may dissolve the NA on the advice of the PM.

questions.prompt: The Objectives Resolution was adopted by the Constituent Assembly in which year?
questions.explanation: It was passed on 12 March 1949 and later made the preamble of the constitutions.

questions.prompt: How many judges sit on the Supreme Court of Pakistan's bench?
options: The Chief Justice plus other judges as fixed by law
questions.explanation: The strength is determined by statute; the CJP presides over the bench.

questions.prompt: Which article protects the right to information?
questions.explanation: Article 19A, added by the 18th Amendment, guarantees the right to information.

questions.prompt: Who appoints the Chief Election Commissioner?
questions.explanation: The CEC is appointed by the President under Article 213.

questions.prompt: Which amendment restored the 1973 Constitution's original parliamentary character?
questions.explanation: The 18th Amendment (2010) abolished the discretionary powers of the President.

questions.prompt: The Senate of Pakistan has how many members?
questions.explanation: After the 25th Amendment, the Senate has 104 members.

questions.prompt: Which body interprets the Constitution in Pakistan?
questions.explanation: The Supreme Court is the final interpreter of the Constitution.

questions.prompt: What does Article 8 of the Constitution declare?
options: Laws inconsistent with fundamental rights are void
questions.explanation: Article 8 nullifies any law that conflicts with fundamental rights.

questions.prompt: Which amendment made Urdu the sole national language?
options: No amendment; it was so from 1973
questions.explanation: Article 251 declared Urdu the national language from the outset of the 1973 Constitution.

questions.prompt: What is the term of office for a Senator?
questions.explanation: Senators serve six-year terms, with half retiring every three years.

questions.prompt: Who presides over joint sittings of the Parliament?
options: The Speaker of the National Assembly
questions.explanation: The Speaker presides over joint sittings under Article 56.

questions.prompt: The concept of 'Provincial Autonomy' was strengthened by which amendment?
questions.explanation: The 18th Amendment devolved 47 subjects to the provinces.

questions.prompt: Who was the first female Speaker of the National Assembly of Pakistan?
questions.explanation: Fahmida Mirza served as Speaker from 2008 to 2013.

questions.prompt: Which constitutional body oversees the federal budget?
questions.explanation: The money bill originates in the National Assembly.

questions.prompt: Article 62 of the Constitution deals with:
options: Qualifications of a member of Parliament
questions.explanation: Article 62 lays down the qualifications for parliamentary membership.

questions.prompt: Who acts as President when the office falls vacant?
questions.explanation: Under Article 49, the Senate Chairman acts as President until a successor is elected.

questions.prompt: The Council of Common Interests was established under which article?
questions.explanation: Article 153 creates the Council of Common Interests.

questions.prompt: How many amendments has the 1973 Constitution undergone so far?
questions.explanation: The Constitution has been amended 26 times, the latest being the 26th Amendment (2024).

questions.prompt: The federal capital territory is governed under which article?
questions.explanation: Article 55 covers the administration of the federal capital, Islamabad.

questions.prompt: Which institution is known as the 'supreme guardian' of the Constitution?
questions.explanation: The Supreme Court acts as the guardian and final interpreter of the Constitution.

questions.prompt: Under Article 63, a member of Parliament is disqualified if he:
options: Is of unsound mind or holds dual nationality
questions.explanation: Article 63 lists grounds of disqualification including unsound mind and dual citizenship.

questions.prompt: The National Finance Commission is constituted under which article?
questions.explanation: Article 160 provides for the National Finance Commission.

questions.prompt: What is the minimum age to become President of Pakistan?
questions.explanation: A presidential candidate must be at least 45 years old under Article 41.

questions.prompt: Which article of the 1973 Constitution deals with the election of the President?
questions.explanation: Article 41 governs the election and qualifications of the President.

questions.prompt: The National Assembly's term is:
questions.explanation: The National Assembly serves a five-year term.

questions.prompt: The 'basic structure doctrine' in Pakistan was discussed in which famous case?
options: Zulfiqar Ali Bhutto vs State (Nusrat Bhutto case context)
questions.explanation: The Supreme Court's 1977 Nusrat Bhutto case addressed the constitutional order.

questions.prompt: Which amendment declared Islam as the state religion?
questions.explanation: The 2nd Amendment (1974) declared Ahmadis non-Muslims; the state religion provision was already in the 1973 Constitution.

questions.prompt: Who is the constitutional head of the federal government?
questions.explanation: The PM is the chief executive under the 1973 Constitution.

questions.prompt: The federal cabinet is appointed by:
options: The President on the PM's advice
questions.explanation: The President appoints the cabinet on the advice of the Prime Minister.

questions.prompt: Article 58(2)(b), which allowed the President to dissolve the NA, was restored by which amendment?
questions.explanation: The 17th Amendment (2003) restored Article 58(2)(b).

questions.prompt: Which body decides on the disqualification of an MNA under Article 63A?
questions.explanation: Article 63A provides for the ECP to decide on defection cases.

questions.prompt: The oath of the Chief Justice of Pakistan is administered by:
questions.explanation: The President administers the oath to the Chief Justice.

questions.prompt: Which amendment set up the National Accountability Bureau (NAB)?
options: No amendment; NAB was created by an ordinance (1999)
questions.explanation: NAB was established by the National Accountability Ordinance 1999.

questions.prompt: How many provinces were recognised in the 1973 Constitution?
questions.explanation: The 1973 Constitution recognised four provinces.

questions.prompt: The right to education (Article 25A) was inserted by:
questions.explanation: Article 25A, added in 2010, guarantees free education for ages 5–16.

questions.prompt: The Federal Shariat Court was established under:
questions.explanation: The Federal Shariat Court was created by the 1973 Constitution.

questions.prompt: Article 245 of the Constitution empowers:
options: The Armed Forces to defend Pakistan when called
questions.explanation: Article 245 deals with the Armed Forces' duty to defend Pakistan.

questions.prompt: Which authority grants assent to a bill passed by Parliament?
questions.explanation: The President gives assent to bills under Article 75.

questions.prompt: The first session of the current Constitution's National Assembly met in:
questions.explanation: The first NA under the 1973 Constitution convened in August 1973.

questions.prompt: The Provincial Assemblies' seats for minorities are reserved under:
questions.explanation: Article 106 provides for minority seats in provincial assemblies.

questions.prompt: The 1956 Constitution of Pakistan was abrogated in which year?
questions.explanation: The 1956 Constitution was abrogated on 7 October 1958 when martial law was declared.

questions.prompt: The 1962 Constitution of Pakistan was enforced in which year?
questions.explanation: The 1962 Constitution came into force on 8 June 1962 under Ayub Khan.

questions.prompt: The 1962 Constitution was abrogated in which year?
questions.explanation: Yahya Khan abrogated the 1962 Constitution and imposed martial law in March 1969.

questions.prompt: The Legal Framework Order (LFO) of 1970 was issued by whom?
questions.explanation: Yahya Khan issued the LFO 1970 to set rules for the general elections.

questions.prompt: The Interim Constitution of Pakistan (1972) was framed under whom?
questions.explanation: The interim constitution was adopted in 1972 under Bhutto's leadership.

questions.prompt: The 1973 Constitution of Pakistan was enforced on which date?
questions.explanation: The 1973 Constitution came into force on 14 August 1973.

questions.prompt: Article 6 of the 1973 Constitution declares what?
options: Acts against the state to be high treason
questions.explanation: Article 6 makes abrogation or subversion of the Constitution high treason.

questions.prompt: Article 9 of the Constitution guarantees?
questions.explanation: Article 9 guarantees no person shall be deprived of life or liberty save by law.

questions.prompt: The right to a fair trial (Article 10A) was inserted by which amendment?
questions.explanation: Article 10A on the right to a fair trial was added by the 18th Amendment (2010).

questions.prompt: Article 14 of the Constitution protects?
questions.explanation: Article 14 protects the dignity of man and the inviolability of privacy.

questions.prompt: Freedom of movement is guaranteed under which Article?
questions.explanation: Article 15 guarantees freedom of movement throughout Pakistan.

questions.prompt: Freedom of association is guaranteed under which Article?
questions.explanation: Article 17 grants the right to form associations and unions.

questions.prompt: Freedom of religion is guaranteed under which Article?
questions.explanation: Article 20 guarantees freedom to profess and practise religion.

questions.prompt: Protection of property rights is provided under which Article?
questions.explanation: Article 24 protects the right to property in accordance with law.

questions.prompt: Article 26 of the Constitution deals with?
options: Non-discrimination in access to public places
questions.explanation: Article 26 prohibits discrimination in access to public places on grounds of race, religion or sex.

questions.prompt: Which amendment introduced the anti-defection law in Pakistan?
questions.explanation: The 14th Amendment (1997) disqualified floor-crossers from membership of assemblies.

questions.prompt: The 13th Amendment (1997) is known for?
options: Abolishing the President's power to dissolve the National Assembly
questions.explanation: The 13th Amendment removed the discretionary power of the President to dissolve the National Assembly.

questions.prompt: The Eighth Amendment, which added Article 58(2)(b), was passed in which year?
questions.explanation: The 8th Amendment (1985) introduced Article 58(2)(b) giving the President power to dissolve the Assembly.

questions.prompt: The 20th Amendment (2012) dealt with?
questions.explanation: The 20th Amendment set rules for caretaker governments and timely elections.

questions.prompt: The 21st Amendment (2015) established?
questions.explanation: The 21st Amendment allowed trial of terrorism cases in military courts.

questions.prompt: The 24th Amendment (2017) is related to?
options: Delimitation of constituencies based on the census
questions.explanation: The 24th Amendment allowed delimitation of constituencies on the basis of the 2017 census.

questions.prompt: The 26th Amendment (2024) is most notable for?
options: Constitutional Benches and a fixed term for the Chief Justice
questions.explanation: The 26th Amendment set up Constitutional Benches and fixed the Chief Justice's term at three years.

questions.prompt: The 27th Amendment (2025) provided for?
options: Extension of military courts under the Army Act
questions.explanation: The 27th Amendment re-enacted provisions extending military courts.

questions.prompt: The Governor of a province is appointed by?
questions.explanation: Under Article 101, the Governor is appointed by the President.

questions.prompt: The Chief Minister of a province is elected by?
questions.explanation: Under Article 130, the Chief Minister is elected by the provincial assembly.

questions.prompt: Caretaker governments in Pakistan are provided for under which Article?
questions.explanation: Article 224 deals with caretaker governments before elections.

questions.prompt: The power to amend the Constitution is vested in Parliament under which Article?
questions.explanation: Article 238 gives Parliament the power to amend the Constitution, with procedure in Article 239.

questions.prompt: How many non-Muslim seats are reserved in the National Assembly?
questions.explanation: Ten seats in the National Assembly are reserved for non-Muslims.

questions.prompt: Senators in Pakistan are elected through?
questions.explanation: Senate members are elected through proportional representation by the provincial assemblies.

questions.prompt: The President of Pakistan must be?
questions.explanation: Under Article 41, the President must be a Muslim of at least 45 years of age.

questions.prompt: The Supreme Judicial Council is empowered to?
questions.explanation: The Supreme Judicial Council investigates and may recommend removal of judges.

questions.prompt: Advisory jurisdiction of the Supreme Court is provided under which Article?
questions.explanation: Under Article 186 the President may refer questions of public importance for the Court's opinion.

questions.prompt: The Supreme Court can exercise suo motu jurisdiction under which Article?
questions.explanation: Article 184(3) allows the Supreme Court to take suo motu action on matters of public importance.

questions.prompt: How many High Courts does Pakistan currently have?
questions.explanation: Pakistan has five High Courts: four provincial and the Islamabad High Court.
